title: Range

compareCandidate.label: Range vs. mean
compareCandidate.description: The mean names a typical value; the range tells how spread out the values are. Two datasets can share a mean but have very different ranges.

plainLanguageExplanation: The range is how spread out a dataset is — the largest value minus the smallest value. For scores 55, 70, 82, 90, the range is 90 − 55 = 35. A small range means the data is bunched together; a large range means it is spread wide. It is a quick, one-number description of spread — but because it only uses two numbers, one far-out outlier can stretch a big range and hide how tight the middle really is.

keyFacts.label: Meaning
keyFacts.value: How spread out the data is

whyItMatters: The range tells you at a glance whether numbers are close together or far apart — from test scores to weather highs. It is the simplest of the spread measures and the natural companion to the mean.
didYouKnow: The range is the 'box that holds all the data' — the full gap covered by the values. Weather forecasters use daily high and low to give you the range of the day.
compareReason: Students see 'average' and 'spread' as the same idea — comparing the central mean with the spread range makes the two jobs of statistics clear.
